messages:
lantern-app-team: Hey team, seeing a sharp p99 increase for our tenant (lantern-prod) since ~13:58 UTC. Users report timeouts and degraded UX. Any quick triage?

sam_support: Thanks for flagging — can you paste a sample request id or api key id? Also which model/route are you hitting?

lantern-app-team: sample request id `r_7b2f9a` — mostly /v1/generate with model 'redwood-large-8k', avg qps ~25, bursts to 120. No config changes on our side.

anya_sre: grabbing tenant metrics now. Can you hold on for a sec? :eyes:

deploy-bot: Notice: autoscaler executed scale_up for pool-gamma at 2026-03-15T13:59:12Z (reason: queue_depth > 85%).

anya_sre: Quick snapshot: queue depth spiked and p99 jumped to ~4.8s at 13:58Z, p95 ~820ms. There's a correlated rise in contention on the priority-lane semaphore for hosts serving embeddings and chat. Possibly noisy neighbor on same host group.

jonah_oncall: Do we have throttle events or per-tenant routing changes? Checking policy logs.

derek_runtime: I see a flurry of long-running KV cache misses for lantern-prod — lots of cold prefix hits. Also a handful of large batched requests (~batch_size=64) from one client ip causing head-of-line.

sam_support: lantern-app-team, any sudden spike in long documents or new embedding pipeline?

lantern-app-team: We did start a new nightly bulk-embed job but it runs at 02:00 UTC normally. Nothing scheduled for 13:50.

anya_sre: Given the evidence, likely a cross-tenant noisy flow — big batched requests + KV churn. Immediate mitigation options: 1) add lantern-prod to the per-tenant priority allowlist to avoid shared batching contention, 2) apply a soft throttle to offending origin (if we can identify single IP), 3) reserve an ephemeral capacity slot (30m) for lantern-prod. Thoughts?

jonah_oncall: We can do ephemeral reservation quickly. Sam, can you confirm customer OK with short downtime/redirect?

sam_support: Reached out to lantern-app-team: they approve ephemeral reservation for 20 minutes while we investigate.

derek_runtime: I'll apply a temporary reservation to their tenant and drop aggressive batching on affected hosts. Running command now:

```
# allocate ephemeral reservation
redwoodctl reservations create --tenant lantern-prod --duration 20m --pool gamma-reserve
```

deploy-bot: Reservation created id `res_9c8` for tenant lantern-prod, expires 2026-03-15T14:20:21Z.

anya_sre: After reservation, p99 fell from ~4.8s -> 560ms within 90s. p95 back to ~700ms. Looks good.

lantern-app-team: Confirming UX improved for our users. Thanks.

sam_support: Logged internal incident and customer notification. We'll keep the reservation while SRE investigates root cause.

anya_sre: Next steps to prevent recurrence: 1) identify offending client IPs and block/bucket — see host logs for top contributors; 2) propose updating tenant QoS rules so lantern-prod gets weighted priority during bursts; 3) recommend customer schedule large batches to off-peak or use our Bulk Embeddings endpoint with reservation semantics.

derek_runtime: I pulled host-side heatmap — one IP `52.14.211.33` accounted for ~42% of large batch requests during spike. Could be internal crawler or misconfigured job. Recommend soft-rate-limit that IP and notify customer of findings.

lantern-app-team: That's not an IP we control. Could it be a partner? We'll investigate but please apply soft limits.

sam_support: Applying soft rate-limit rule (no hard drop) to reduce batching impact while we validate identity.

```
# example soft-rate-limit mutation
redwoodctl tenants update lantern-prod --soft-throttle "ip:52.14.211.33=10rps"
```

any_sre_reaction_note: :thumbsup: (internal)

anya_sre: Also adding a bespoke allowlist entry for lantern-prod on pool-gamma to avoid placement with noisy tenants during the next 24h. This is temporary until we tune QoS.

deploy-bot: Placement hint applied: `allowlist:lantern-prod -> pool-gamma:24h`

jonah_oncall: I'll follow up on autoscaler logs to ensure we weren't underprovisioned; autoscaler did trigger but scale-up lag may have contributed.

sam_support: Finalizing customer comms: we've applied a temporary reservation and rate-limited the suspicious source. We're continuing investigation (SRE + runtime). We'll share root-cause when available. Anything else to add?

lantern-app-team: No, that's perfect. Please keep us posted.

anya_sre: Opening a follow-up ticket for QoS policy changes and improved detection for large-batch noisy flows. Reference: INC-2026-314.

sam_support: Closing loop with customer and marking this thread as mitigated. If performance regresses before reservations expire, ping @oncall. :white_check_mark:

lantern-app-team: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick turnaround!
